attitude.simple: the way you think and behave
attitude.natural: His attitude changed once he understood the reason.
attitude.positive: A good attitude turns an ordinary opportunity into a great one.
attitude.leadership: A leader's attitude sets the mood of the whole team.
attitude.factual: A positive attitude was found to improve recovery after surgery.
attitude.general: She has a cheerful attitude towards chores.

education.natural: He valued education because it had changed his own life.
education.positive: Education opens doors that cannot be closed again.
education.leadership: A leader invests in the education of others, not only his own.
education.factual: The Right to Education Act was passed in 2009.
education.general: Her education was paid for by a scholarship.

team.natural: He trusted the team and did his own part well.
team.positive: A good team makes each person stronger than he is alone.
team.leadership: A leader builds the team before building the plan.
team.factual: The team completed the exercise in the shortest time.

tough.natural: The task was tough, but he kept at it.
tough.positive: Tough times reveal who your real friends are.
tough.leadership: A leader stays tough on the problem and gentle with people.
tough.factual: The route was tough because of the loose gravel.
tough.general: It has been a tough week at work.

regular.simple: happening at fixed times or in a pattern
regular.natural: He kept a regular routine even on holidays.
regular.positive: Regular small efforts beat occasional big ones.
regular.leadership: A leader keeps regular hours so the team can plan.
regular.factual: The regular check is done every third day.
regular.general: He is a regular customer at the bakery.

problem.natural: He wrote the problem down before trying to solve it.
problem.positive: Every problem carries the seed of a better method.
problem.leadership: A leader absorbs the problem instead of passing it down.
problem.factual: The problem was traced to a loose connection.
problem.general: The problem is that the shop closes early.

decision.natural: He made the decision and informed the team.
decision.positive: A decision made early can be changed; none made cannot.
decision.leadership: A leader takes the final decision and stands by it.
decision.factual: The committee's decision was announced in the evening.
decision.general: Renovating the kitchen was a good decision.

curiosity.simple: the wish to know or learn
curiosity.natural: His curiosity made him open the old radio.
curiosity.positive: Curiosity keeps the mind young and learning.
curiosity.leadership: A leader encourages curiosity instead of punishing questions.
curiosity.factual: Curiosity is what drove most early scientific discoveries.
curiosity.general: Curiosity made the cat climb the shelf.

competition.natural: He treated the competition as a chance to test himself.
competition.leadership: A leader keeps competition fair and celebrates effort.
competition.factual: The competition had over two hundred entries.
competition.general: There is stiff competition for that seat.

father.natural: He called his father before making the final choice.
father.positive: A father's quiet example teaches more than his advice.
father.leadership: A leader feels as responsible for his team as a father for his family.
father.factual: His father served in the army for twenty years.
father.general: My father taught me to ride a cycle.

stamina.natural: He saved his stamina for the final stretch.
stamina.positive: Stamina is built by small efforts repeated daily.
stamina.leadership: A leader paces the team so stamina lasts the full distance.
stamina.factual: Long-distance running mainly builds stamina and mental strength.
stamina.general: The hill climb tested everyone's stamina.

death.natural: He thought about death and held life more carefully.
death.positive: The reality of death teaches us to value the time we have.
death.leadership: A leader protects life and takes the risks himself.
death.factual: Road accidents cause over a lakh deaths in India every year.
death.general: The death of the old tree changed the shade of the courtyard.

struggle.natural: He struggled with the rope before the team pulled together.
struggle.positive: The struggle is where real strength is made.
struggle.leadership: A leader struggles beside the team, never above it.
struggle.factual: The struggle for independence lasted almost a century.
struggle.general: I struggle to wake up early in winter.

war.simple: armed conflict between groups or countries
war.natural: He studied war to understand its human cost.
war.positive: Understanding war is the first step to preventing it.
war.leadership: A leader prepares for war but works for peace.
war.factual: The Second World War ended in 1945.
war.general: The museum has many pictures from the war.

faith.natural: He kept his faith and kept working.
faith.positive: Faith gives calm when the outcome is still unknown.
faith.leadership: A leader earns the team's faith by keeping his word.
faith.factual: The soldiers had faith in their training and their leader.
faith.general: I have faith that things will settle down.

system.simple: a set of parts that work together
system.natural: He learned the system before trying to change it.
system.positive: A good system makes the right action easy.
system.leadership: A leader improves the system instead of blaming people.
system.factual: The alert system worked and warned the village in time.
system.general: The ticket system is down today.

solve.natural: He solved the problem quietly before anyone noticed.
solve.positive: Most problems are solved by the simplest workable step.
solve.leadership: A leader solves what is blocking the team first.
solve.factual: The engineers solved the fault within two hours.
solve.general: Can you solve this crossword clue?

detail.natural: He checked every detail before signing.
detail.positive: Care for detail separates good work from great work.
detail.leadership: A leader checks important details without slowing the team.
detail.factual: The report covered every detail of the inspection.
detail.general: The plan is fine; do not worry about the detail.

together.natural: They worked together and finished early.
together.positive: Together we can do what none of us can alone.
together.leadership: A leader brings people together instead of taking sides.
together.factual: The two villages built the bridge together.

difficult.natural: The climb looked difficult, so he started slowly.
difficult.positive: A difficult task done well is worth more than five easy ones.
difficult.leadership: A leader takes the difficult part himself.
difficult.factual: The road was difficult after the rain.
difficult.general: It is difficult to choose between the two.

respect.simple: to think well of someone and treat them well
respect.natural: He respected every person, whatever their rank.
respect.positive: Respect given freely returns without being asked.
respect.leadership: A leader respects the team first and expects it back.
respect.factual: The officer was respected for his fairness.
respect.general: Respect your elders, but learn from everyone.

nation.natural: He felt proud of the nation's achievements.
nation.positive: A nation grows when its people work together.
nation.leadership: A leader serves the nation before party or self.
nation.factual: The nation celebrated its independence day with a parade.
nation.general: The whole nation watched the match.

peace.natural: He found peace in the early morning walk.
peace.positive: Peace built on justice lasts; peace bought by silence does not.
peace.leadership: A leader keeps peace inside the team before asking it of others.
peace.factual: India has contributed to many peacekeeping missions.
peace.general: There is peace and quiet after the festival.

compromise.simple: a solution where both sides give a little
compromise.natural: Both sides compromised without losing the main point.
compromise.positive: A fair compromise saves the relationship for a better day.
compromise.leadership: A leader compromises on method but not on standards.
compromise.factual: The border agreement was a compromise between two claims.
compromise.general: We compromised and picked two restaurants.

challenge.simple: a difficult task that tests you
challenge.natural: He accepted the challenge and started that evening.
challenge.positive: Every challenge is a chance to prove yourself to yourself.
challenge.leadership: A leader accepts the challenge and carries the risk.
challenge.factual: The challenge was to finish the march with a full pack.
challenge.general: The new timetable is a challenge for all of us.

impossible.natural: He thought it was impossible until he tried a new route.
impossible.positive: The impossible usually takes a longer way round.
impossible.leadership: A leader turns an impossible task into a series of possible steps.
impossible.factual: It is impossible to cross the river in the monsoon.
impossible.general: Getting all four of us free on Sunday is impossible.

rights.simple: what a person is fairly allowed to have
rights.natural: He stood up for the rights of the weaker worker.
rights.positive: Rights respected today prevent suffering tomorrow.
rights.leadership: A leader respects the rights of the people he leads.
rights.factual: The Constitution guarantees fundamental rights to every citizen.
rights.general: You have every right to ask for a receipt.

careless.natural: The careless mistake could have cost the team the match.
careless.positive: Careless habits can be replaced by simple checklists.
careless.leadership: A leader corrects careless work before it reaches the customer.
careless.factual: The report was careless with dates and was returned.
careless.general: It was careless of me to leave the keys inside.

prosperity.natural: The family worked hard and made its prosperity itself.
prosperity.positive: Prosperity shared across the village is prosperity that lasts.
prosperity.leadership: A leader builds prosperity for the many, not the few.
prosperity.factual: Trade and education drove the region's prosperity.
prosperity.general: The market reflects the city's prosperity.

responsible.natural: He accepted he was responsible for the mix-up.
responsible.positive: Taking responsibility is the mark of a person you can trust.
responsible.leadership: A leader is responsible for the team's mistakes before he is responsible for its wins.
responsible.factual: The officer responsible for the route was changed.
responsible.general: I am responsible for feeding the dog.

advance.natural: He advanced slowly and kept a steady pace.
advance.positive: Advance in small steps and you will not fall back.
advance.leadership: A leader advances only after making sure the way is clear.
advance.factual: The team advanced two kilometres before nightfall.

lead.simple: to guide others or be in front
lead.natural: He led from the front without raising his voice.
lead.positive: The best way to lead is to make others feel capable.
lead.leadership: A leader leads by example, then by instruction.
lead.factual: India leads the world in digital payments.
lead.general: This road leads to the station.

character.simple: the qualities that make a person
character.natural: His character showed in how he treated the waiters.
character.positive: Character is built in small choices, not big speeches.
character.leadership: A leader's character is tested most on bad days.
character.factual: The school gives prizes for character and conduct.
character.general: She has a strong character and never gives up.

newspaper.simple: a paper printed with the news
newspaper.natural: He read the newspaper before starting his day.
newspaper.positive: A newspaper habit keeps the mind awake to the world.
newspaper.leadership: A leader reads beyond the headlines before forming a view.
newspaper.factual: The newspaper carries news in twelve local editions.
newspaper.general: The newspaper is delivered at six.

programme.natural: He joined the programme to learn first aid.
programme.positive: A good programme leaves people better than it found them.
programme.leadership: The leader designed the programme around the team's weaknesses.
programme.factual: The training programme runs for six weeks.
programme.general: The music programme starts at eight.

tiredness.natural: Tiredness slowed him down, but he finished the task.
tiredness.positive: Rest is part of work, not a break from it.
tiredness.leadership: A leader notices tiredness in the team before it causes mistakes.
tiredness.factual: Tiredness was the main cause of the early errors.
tiredness.general: Tiredness caught up with me after lunch.

conference.simple: a meeting to discuss a subject
conference.natural: He spoke briefly at the conference and listened more.
conference.positive: A good conference sends everyone home with one useful idea.
conference.leadership: A leader makes the team feel free to speak at a conference.
conference.factual: The conference was attended by two hundred delegates.
conference.general: The conference call is at ten tomorrow.

correct.natural: He checked twice and found the correct answer.
correct.positive: Being corrected early is a gift, not an insult.
correct.leadership: A leader corrects the error quietly and the person publicly never.
correct.factual: The correct pressure for the tyre is listed in the manual.
correct.general: Please correct me if I am wrong.

enjoy.natural: He enjoyed the walk even in the rain.
enjoy.positive: Enjoy the work and it takes less effort.
enjoy.leadership: A leader makes sure the team enjoys the journey, not only the result.
enjoy.factual: The children enjoyed the museum visit the most.

leader.simple: a person who guides a group
leader.natural: The leader listened first and spoke last.
leader.positive: A good leader makes other leaders, not followers.
leader.leadership: A leader takes the blame and gives away the credit.
leader.factual: The leader of the expedition had climbed the peak twice before.
leader.general: Every group needs a leader for the trip.

alert.natural: He stayed alert even during the quiet hours.
alert.positive: An alert mind prevents most accidents.
alert.leadership: A leader keeps the team alert without keeping them afraid.
alert.factual: The guard was alert and spotted the movement at once.
alert.general: Stay alert on the road at night.

method.natural: He used a simple method and stuck to it.
method.positive: A clear method removes confusion under pressure.
method.leadership: A leader improves the method after hearing the team.
method.factual: The new method cut the repair time by half.
method.general: There must be a better method for packing.

defeat.natural: He accepted the defeat and asked for a rematch.
defeat.positive: Defeat teaches faster than victory if you let it.
defeat.leadership: A leader absorbs defeat and protects the team's confidence.
defeat.factual: The army suffered a defeat at the river crossing.
defeat.general: The defeat in the final was hard to take.

coward.simple: someone who runs from danger or duty
coward.natural: He refused to be called a coward and stepped forward.
coward.positive: Nobody is born a coward; courage can be practised.
coward.leadership: A leader never shames a frightened person into action.
coward.factual: The word coward describes someone who avoids danger out of fear.
coward.general: It is being a coward to let a friend take the blame.

governor.simple: the head of a state or an institution
governor.natural: The governor visited the flood-hit district.
governor.positive: A good governor listens to the smallest village.
governor.leadership: A governor leads by visiting the problem, not just reading reports.
governor.factual: The Governor is appointed by the President of India.
governor.general: The governor met the students at the function.

travel.simple: to go from one place to another
travel.natural: He travelled by train to see his family.
travel.positive: Travel teaches more than books about how others live.
travel.leadership: A leader travels light and keeps the team together.
travel.factual: The journey by road takes about six hours.
travel.general: I travel to the city twice a week.

democracy.natural: He valued the right to vote in a democracy.
democracy.positive: Democracy grows stronger each time people vote thoughtfully.
democracy.leadership: A leader in a democracy listens even to those who did not vote for him.
democracy.factual: India is the largest democracy in the world.
democracy.general: The debate was a good example of democracy at work.

irresponsible.simple: not taking proper care or duty
irresponsible.natural: He realised the irresponsible choice had cost the team time.
irresponsible.positive: An irresponsible habit can be replaced with one small rule.
irresponsible.leadership: A leader corrects irresponsible behaviour before it spreads.
irresponsible.factual: Irresponsible driving caused most of the accidents last year.
irresponsible.general: It was irresponsible to leave the gate open.

rigid.simple: stiff, or not willing to change
rigid.natural: The rigid plan broke as soon as the weather changed.
rigid.positive: Be firm on values and flexible on methods.
rigid.leadership: A rigid leader loses good ideas; a flexible one keeps them.
rigid.factual: The frame is rigid enough to carry the load.
rigid.general: Her timetable is too rigid for a holiday.

persuade.simple: to make someone agree by talking
persuade.natural: He persuaded the crowd to step back calmly.
persuade.positive: Persuasion by listening works better than pressure.
persuade.leadership: A leader persuades the team to accept a hard decision.
persuade.factual: The officer persuaded the family to move to higher ground.
persuade.general: She persuaded me to try the new route.

hate.natural: He hated waste and saved everything usable.
hate.positive: Hate used against a bad habit is useful.
hate.leadership: A leader hates the problem, never the person.
hate.factual: The campaign asks people to hate discrimination, not people.
hate.general: I hate waiting in long queues.

help.simple: to make things easier for someone
help.positive: Help offered early is worth more than rescue later.
help.leadership: A leader helps the team finish rather than finishing first.
help.factual: The villagers helped clear the road after the landslide.
help.general: Can you help me carry these boxes?

understand.natural: He understood the worry behind the sharp words.
understand.positive: Understanding the other person solves half the conflict.
understand.leadership: A leader understands the problem before giving the order.
understand.factual: The students understood the lesson after the example.
understand.general: I understand how you feel about this.

revolution.simple: a complete change, often by force
revolution.natural: He read about the revolution and its costs.
revolution.positive: A revolution of daily habits changes a life quietly.
revolution.leadership: A leader brings change with explanation, not only with force.
revolution.factual: The industrial revolution began in the eighteenth century.
revolution.general: The new phone caused a small revolution at home.

adventure.natural: He said yes to the adventure and packed lightly.
adventure.positive: An adventure with preparation is safer and more fun.
adventure.leadership: A leader takes the risk himself so the adventure stays safe for others.
adventure.factual: The trek was an adventure of five days through the forest.
adventure.general: Driving in the rain felt like an adventure.

goal.natural: He wrote his goal where he could see it daily.
goal.positive: A clear goal makes courage easier.
goal.leadership: A leader sets the goal and then lets the team own the method.
goal.factual: The goal was to complete the march in twelve hours.
goal.general: My goal is to save for a new cycle.

accommodate.simple: to make room for or adjust to
accommodate.natural: He accommodated the extra guests without complaint.
accommodate.positive: A willingness to accommodate keeps a group together.
accommodate.leadership: A leader accommodates a genuine need without lowering standards.
accommodate.factual: The hall can accommodate three hundred people.
accommodate.general: Can the car accommodate five of us?

teacher.natural: He remembered the teacher who believed in him.
teacher.positive: A good teacher asks better questions than he answers.
teacher.leadership: A leader is a teacher first and a commander second.
teacher.factual: The school has one teacher for every thirty students.
teacher.general: My teacher gave us extra time for the project.

bank.simple: a place that keeps money, or land beside a river
bank.natural: He went to the bank before it closed.
bank.positive: Small savings kept safely in a bank build security.
bank.leadership: A leader plans the team's money with the same care as his own.
bank.factual: The bank opens at ten and closes at four.
bank.general: We sat on the river bank and watched the birds.

self respect.natural: He kept his self respect by telling the truth.
self respect.positive: Self respect is protected by small honest choices.
self respect.leadership: A leader protects the self respect of every person he corrects.
self respect.factual: The workshop focused on discipline and self respect.
self respect.general: She walked away to keep her self respect.
